About

My work spans infectious disease epidemiology, antimicrobial resistance, immunization, health systems research, traditional medicine and health-seeking behaviour, population mental health, and digital health. I bring together public health practice, interdisciplinary research, and education to address complex health challenges.

I hold a PhD in Medical Microbiology from Federal University Wukari, an MSc in Public Health from Oxford Brookes University, and a BSc in Microbiology from Ambrose Alli University. I have served as a Postdoctoral Visitor at York University since 1 December 2025, alongside my teaching appointment at Federal University Wukari.

Beyond the Research

A few personal photographs.

Research

Digital mental health & AI

Exploring multimodal approaches to supporting newcomer mental health, including physiological, behavioural and self-reported data, with attention to fairness, explainability and privacy.

Infectious disease epidemiology

Research on Salmonella epidemiology, antimicrobial resistance, pathogen characterization and disease prevention.

Immunization & health systems

Evidence synthesis and public health practice in immunization, health systems strengthening, and community-based health interventions.

Traditional medicine & health-seeking behaviour

Investigating the socioeconomic and cultural factors shaping traditional medicine use, healthcare choices, and access to equitable, culturally responsive public health services.

Teaching & mentorship

My teaching covers epidemiology and public health, medical and veterinary microbiology, pharmaceutical microbiology, virology, immunology, and research methods. I emphasize student-centred learning, critical thinking, inclusive participation, and the application of scientific knowledge to public health practice.

I have supported undergraduate and postgraduate research supervision and interdisciplinary student mentorship.
